project: Enabling Exploratory Learning for Manufacturing System Performance with AI-Agents and Digital Twins (NIST MSR, Tilbury/Barton)
purpose: Structured comparison of agent-based manufacturing frameworks against the Kovalenko/Tilbury/Barton reference framework [7,8,10]. NOT a narrative survey: proposal S2.2 explicitly declines to produce 'yet another survey of agent-based approaches to manufacturing [6,23,24,27]'.

extraction_contract.evidence_rule: Every field in blocks A-I MUST be returned as an object {value, evidence_quote, page, confidence}. If no supporting text exists in the paper, value MUST be 'not_reported' and evidence_quote MUST be null. Never infer a value from the paper's general topic, venue, or title.
extraction_contract.quote_limits: evidence_quote must be a verbatim span of at most 25 words copied from the source PDF. Longer spans are rejected by the validator.
extraction_contract.no_counting_rule: The extracting model must NOT compute totals, percentages, or cross-paper comparisons. All aggregation is performed deterministically in pandas. Basis: proposal S3.3 reports that foundation models 'exhibit inconsistencies in numerical accuracy' and require 'validation through deterministic tools or human oversight' [26].

IDENT.label: Identification
IDENT.proposal_basis: Bookkeeping; enables the scripted citation-resolution check (no fabricated references in a NIST deliverable).

paper_id.note: OpenAlex work ID from corpus CSV

seed_role_links.note: which seed roles this paper was reached from; copied from corpus CSV, not extracted

A_DEFINITION.label: Definition and terminology
A_DEFINITION.proposal_basis: S2.2: 'analyze the different definitions of manufacturing agents, the characteristics they contain (both required and optional)'. S2.4: 'make recommendations on clarifying, expanding, and aligning terms, definitions and ontologies' [16,29,30].

agent_definition_verbatim.prompt: Quote the paper's own definition of what an agent is. If it adopts a definition from another work, record that and name the source.

agent_term_used.note: Terminology divergence is itself a finding; feeds the S2.4 ontology recommendation.

agent_entity_types.proposal_basis: Project description: 'each resource in the system with its own AI-agent ... every part (or batch of parts) to be produced also has its own AI-agent [7,9,10]'. Part-agent vs resource-agent coverage is the axis of interest.

B_ARCHITECTURE.label: Internal architecture (KB / decision maker / communication manager)
B_ARCHITECTURE.proposal_basis: S3.2: 'Agents typically include a knowledge base (with beliefs, desires and intentions), a decision maker and a communication manager that can interact with other agents; see Figure 5.' The proposal supplies this triad, so it is the schema backbone rather than an invented taxonomy.

decision_mechanism.proposal_basis: S3.2: 'the decision making of specific agents is typically rule-based reasoning ... it is difficult to scale these reasoners to larger systems'. The rule-based share of this column is the scalability argument.

decision_scalability_discussed.prompt: Does the paper address how its decision mechanism scales with number of agents/constraints?

C_MEMORY.label: Memory requirements
C_MEMORY.proposal_basis: S2.2, verbatim research question: 'identifying the specific memory requirements--capturing both historical asset data and real-time environmental contexts'. This block is one of the two named Phase II focus areas and is weighted accordingly.

memory_historical.prompt: What historical data about its own physical asset does the agent retain?

memory_realtime.prompt: How does the agent obtain real-time environmental context?

memory_persists_across_episodes.prompt: Does anything the agent learns or records survive past the end of a single production run/episode?

memory_requirements_stated.prompt: Does the paper explicitly argue what an agent MUST remember? Direct input to the S2.2 'essential components' question.

D_COMMUNICATION.label: Communication dynamics
D_COMMUNICATION.proposal_basis: S2.2, verbatim: 'determining how to optimize communication dynamics between interacting agents'. Second of the two named Phase II focus areas.

negotiation_mechanism.proposal_basis: S2.2 requires the agent to 'negotiate on behalf of its physical counterpart to achieve a desired goal'; [9] is the dynamic resource task negotiation prior work.

comm_cost_analyzed.prompt: Does the paper measure or bound message volume, bandwidth, or latency?
comm_cost_analyzed.note: Low positive rate expected. A near-empty column is the evidence that 'optimize communication dynamics' (S2.2) is an open problem rather than a solved one.

handles_comm_failure.prompt: Dropped messages, latency, partial network partition.

E_LEARNING.label: Learning and exploration
E_LEARNING.proposal_basis: S3.2: 'This project will explore (through a landscape literature survey) when and how the agent-based frameworks that have been proposed for manufacturing systems are able to dynamically learn through exploration'. S2.2: prior agents 'could learn about their environment through communicating with other agents, [but] were not able to explore beyond their pre-defined environment'. This block carries the project's central gap argument.

explores_beyond_predefined_env.prompt: Can the agent acquire capabilities, processes, or environment structure that were NOT enumerated at design time? Answer 'yes' only with explicit textual support. Learning parameters over a fixed action/resource set is 'no'.
explores_beyond_predefined_env.note: PRIMARY DISCRIMINATOR. S2.2 and S3.2 both frame the research gap in exactly these terms. Expect a strong majority of 'no'; that distribution is the finding justifying the Phase II case study.

learning_quality_measured.proposal_basis: S3.2: 'The quality of the learning will also be assessed and measured.'

simulation_model_source.proposal_basis: S2.2: 'since resource DTs contain models that could be used for simulations, an AI-agent may extract copies of these models and orchestrate them together in a combined simulation'. Whether anyone already does this is a direct literature question.

foundation_model_role.proposal_basis: S2.2: 'Queries to a manufacturing foundation model [11,35] may help guide the simulation and inform the exploration'. S3.3 and [26] set expectations for what these models can and cannot do.

foundation_model_limitations_reported.prompt: Any reported failure mode of the LLM/FM used. Feeds the Report 2 failure taxonomy.

F_DT_COUPLING.label: Relationship to digital twins
F_DT_COUPLING.proposal_basis: S2.2: 'In our view, the AI-agent will communicate with the DTs, but will not be incorporated into the DTs (see Figure 2).' Conflation of agent and DT in the literature is a boundary finding, and Phase III question (1) asks whether a DT can be used to auto-generate an agent.

agent_dt_coupling.note: 'agent_and_dt_conflated' is expected to be common and is directly reportable against the proposal's stated separation.

dt_provides_uncertainty.proposal_basis: S3.1 definition [20]: 'The output of the DT (either an estimate or prediction about its physical twin) must be accompanied by a level of confidence, or uncertainty.' Papers calling something a DT without UQ diverge from the reference definition.

dt_generation_from_agent_or_vice_versa.proposal_basis: S2.3 Phase III question (1), verbatim: 'If a Digital Twin for an asset exists, can that be used (together with AI Tools) to automatically generate an AI-agent for the asset? And vice-versa?'

G_VALIDATION_METRICS.label: Validation maturity and manufacturing metrics
G_VALIDATION_METRICS.proposal_basis: S1 establishes the four-tier maturity ladder: 'Some are conceptual frameworks, with colorful graphics and block diagrams. Other frameworks have been implemented in simulation, with varying levels of fidelity. A few case studies with physical hardware have been executed in laboratory environments, and some have been demonstrated on factory floors.' S3.2: 'one focus of the survey will be on the manufacturing metrics (e.g., quality, throughput, reliability) that the frameworks are able to demonstrate.'

validation_level.note: Ladder taken verbatim from proposal S1.

disruption_types_handled.proposal_basis: S2.2: prior work 'demonstrated how the ensemble of agents can work together to react to disruptions that may occur [7]'.

system_scale.note: Numbers copied verbatim from the paper only. The extracting model must not estimate; use null when unstated.

H_STANDARDS.label: Standards and ontology alignment
H_STANDARDS.proposal_basis: S2.4: 'we will consider how the data types that we employ are defined in the latest manufacturing operations standards efforts [16,29,30]. As appropriate, we will make recommendations on clarifying, expanding, and aligning terms, definitions and ontologies.' S2.1 names ISA-95 [18] and Asset Administration Shell [33].

I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE.label: Delta against the Kovalenko/Tilbury/Barton framework
I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE.proposal_basis: S2.2, verbatim: 'extract the features that are common with our definition, as well as those that differ'. S2: 'summarize what are the necessary (and common) features of each framework that can enable the vision we propose'. This block IS the deliverable; everything above feeds it.
I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE.reference_framework: Kovalenko, Tilbury, Barton (2019), 'The model-based product agent: A control oriented architecture for intelligent products in multi-agent manufacturing systems', Control Engineering Practice 86:105-117 [proposal ref 10], with [7] and [8].

features_divergent.prompt: What this framework has or does that the reference framework does not, or vice versa. Be specific and cite the text.

essential_component_claims.prompt: Does the paper argue that any component is NECESSARY (not merely useful) for a manufacturing agent? Quote the claim.
essential_component_claims.proposal_basis: S2.2: 'determine the essential components an AI-agent requires to serve as an effective representative of its physical counterpart'.

static_vs_dynamic_structure.proposal_basis: S3.2: 'Even in our prior work [10], the agents can communicate to learn about their environment, although their structure was static.' Papers with dynamic structure are the highest-value reads.

J_EXTRACTION_META.label: Extraction provenance
J_EXTRACTION_META.proposal_basis: S1.1: 'with humans (students and advisors) guiding the search and reporting the findings'. S2.2 second report: 'summarize how the AI tools were successful (or not)'. S3.3: FM outputs are 'sensitive to input formulation', so prompt identity is experimental apparatus and must be recorded.

prompt_hash.note: sha256 of the exact extraction prompt used

fields_corrected.note: field paths the human changed; this array is the raw material for the per-field error profile in Report 2

aggregation_targets.note: Cross-tabs computed deterministically in pandas, never by an LLM. Each maps to a Report 1 section.
aggregation_targets.R1_S2_necessary_vs_optional: frequency of has_knowledge_base / decision_mechanism / has_communication_manager, split by validation_level
aggregation_targets.R1_S3_memory_and_communication: memory_historical x memory_realtime; comm_protocol x negotiation_mechanism; comm_cost_analyzed rate
aggregation_targets.R1_S4_learning_and_exploration: explores_beyond_predefined_env x learning_type x validation_level; learning_quality_measured rate
aggregation_targets.R1_S7_gaps: intersection of explores_beyond_predefined_env=yes AND validation_level in {lab_hardware, factory_floor} - expected to be near-empty and to justify the Phase II case study
aggregation_targets.R2_method: human_verified rate, fields_corrected frequency per field, screening kappa, failure taxonomy
